source: CARDI (Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute) / វិទ្យាស្ថានស្រាវជ្រាវ និងអភិវឌ្ឍន៍កសិកម្មកម្ពុជា, presentation 'ផលិតកម្មគ្រាប់ពូជ គុណភាព និង ចំណាត់ថ្នាក់' (Seed Production, Quality, and Classification), prepared by Mr. Sang Laiyheng, Deputy Director of the Seed Multiplication Office (Tel: 012 952 801; Email: s_layheng@yahoo.com), dated December 1, 2014.
text:
CARDI describes the field process for producing each class of seed as follows.

Nucleus Seed (400-500 'kur', a panicle/plant-row unit) is the starting point: individual panicles are selected from a source population and, the following season, each is grown out as a separate row (hill) in the field so breeders can compare their offspring side by side. Rows/hills that show characteristics different from the others are discarded; rows with matching, uniform characteristics are combined together. The combined grain from the accepted rows becomes Breeder Seed.

Breeder Seed (BS) is produced by a team of plant breeders starting from Nucleus Seed. About 400-500 individual panicle rows are taken from the nucleus seed source and transplanted out in the field (spread over multiple planting rounds), with each row about 4-5 meters long. Any row displaying characteristics different from the rest is rogued out; rows with matching characteristics are harvested and combined. The resulting grain is Breeder Seed.

Foundation Seed (FS) is produced using Breeder Seed as the planting source, transplanted in rows with one seedling per hill; the harvested grain is Foundation Seed.

Registered Seed (RS) is produced from Foundation Seed.

Certified Seed (CS) is produced from Registered Seed.

Foundation Seed is produced only at dedicated seed multiplication stations, while Registered Seed and Certified Seed may be produced on farmers' fields under the monitoring and inspection of seed-production technicians.

Graded Seed (GS) is produced from Foundation Seed or from pure seed of other classes, without fully maintaining the strict isolation/inspection regime used for the classes above; field practice for Graded Seed resembles ordinary rice production (2-3 seedlings per hill) but must still follow other seed-quality principles.

Multi-year multiplication scheme: because each class must be grown out for at least one season from the class above it, CARDI's training material shows a staggered, rolling multi-year pipeline. In Year 1 the original source variety (labeled 'ពូជ A') is grown to produce Breeder Seed. In Year 2 that Breeder Seed is grown to produce Foundation Seed, while a fresh batch of Breeder Seed is also started. In Year 3 the Foundation Seed produces Registered Seed, the newer Breeder Seed produces a new batch of Foundation Seed, and another fresh Breeder Seed batch is started. This staggered pattern continues through Year 6, by which time the pipeline is simultaneously producing Graded Seed, Certified Seed, Registered Seed, Foundation Seed, and Breeder Seed in parallel from batches started in different years -- keeping a continuous supply of every seed class available every year once the pipeline is fully established.
